holding_summary: Trover action concerning a mortgagee's removal of distillery fixtures (copper stills, kettles) and their subsequent distress for rent by the landlord's bailiff; the court held the removed articles were personal property once severed and were properly distrained within the statutory period.
notes: Distress/fixtures case involving a distillery; no bearing on lodging, boarding, or short-term letting of dwellings.

holding_summary: Ejectment case addressing whether a vendee in possession under a parol purchase contract is entitled to notice to quit; the court surveys notice-to-quit doctrine and holds vendor-vendee relationships are an exception to the general notice requirement.
notes: Notice-to-quit/vendor-vendee ejectment doctrine regarding farmland; unrelated to lodging or boarding practice.

holding_summary: Forcible entry and detainer prosecution over a parol farm lease (six acres let for fencing as rent); the court held a void parol term still creates a tenancy for years within the meaning of the forcible-entry statute, and threats of bodily harm can constitute forcible detainer.
notes: Farm tenancy/forcible detainer case; no lodging, boarding, or dwelling-letting issue.

holding_summary: Dispute among tenants in common over whether one co-tenant's proportion of rents, collected by an agent purportedly acting under void letters of guardianship, could be set off against a separate debt; the court held the remedy lay in an action of account or bill in equity, not set-off.
notes: Guardianship/tenants-in-common accounting dispute. Mentions in passing that the agent was authorized to lease the premises 'to fit... for a tavern,' but the holding concerns set-off and account remedies, not the legal character or regulation of lodging/boarding letting.

court: New York Court for the Correction of Errors
holding_summary: Where the lessor was guilty of habitually bringing lewd women into other apartments under the same roof as the demised premises, causing nocturnal noise and disturbance, the court held this was evidence of a constructive eviction sufficient to go to the jury under a plea of eviction, barring the landlord's recovery of rent even absent a physical entry and expulsion.

quotes.text: two rooms upon the second floor and two rooms upon the third floor whereof had- been leased to the' defendant

Where the lessor was guilty of habitually bringing lewd women under the same roof with the demised premises, though in an apartment not demised, by which nocturnal noise and disturbance were made; and, in consequence, the lessee quitted the premises and remained away with his family; held, that this was evidence to go to the jury under a plea of eviction by the landlord, in answer to a declaration for the rent; and that the jury mighty upon such evidence, find the plea true; and the lessor would thereby be barred of his rent, the same as on an actual or physical entry and expulsion of the tenant.
This is, in its nature, a condition precedent to the payment of rent; and whether the possession was peaceable and quiet, was clearly a question of fact for the jury.

notes: The house was physically divided between rooms occupied by the landlord (first floor) and rooms leased to the tenant (second and third floors) -- a householder letting portions of his own dwelling, treated throughout the opinions as an ordinary lease governed by standard covenants (rent, quiet enjoyment). Central holding is constructive-eviction doctrine, not the legality of the letting itself; polarity is inferred from the court's unquestioning ordinary-lease framing of the arrangement rather than an explicit ruling on legitimacy.

holding_summary: The court held that property belonging to boarders at taverns or boarding houses is not liable to distress for rent owed by the tavern or boarding-house keeper, even though the property is in the keeper's possession and actual use by the boarders' permission and without the landlord's consent.

quotes.text: The property of boarders at taverns or boarding houses is not liable to distress for rent, although such property is not in their possession, but in the possession and actual use of the tenant, by their permission, and without the consent of the landlord.

The property of boarders at taverns or boarding houses is not liable to distress for rent, although such property is not in their possession, but in the possession and actual use of the tenant, by their permission, and without the consent of the landlord.

notes: Court for the Correction of Errors reversed on a procedural ground (verdict already found for plaintiff below) but a majority of members separately adopted a resolution protecting boarders' property from distress for the innkeeper/boarding-house keeper's rent -- directly favorable to boarder status. Duration of the boarders' occupancy is not specified in the excerpt.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Ejectment for breach of a lease covenant limiting the lessee to one tenant or family per 100 acres; the court held that persons occupying parcels for a year on crop shares were 'tenants' within the covenant, and more than the permitted number rendered the lease void.
notes: Agricultural share-cropping tenancy and lease-forfeiture case; concerns farm tenants, not lodging or boarding of dwellings.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Trespass action by a lessor against a sub-tenant at will who removed a house he had built on the demised premises; the court held the lessor could not maintain trespass quare clausum fregit absent actual possession at the time of the alleged injury.
notes: Trespass/fixtures dispute over a sub-tenant's removal of a building he erected; no bearing on lodging or boarding regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Replevin/avowry dispute between two claimants over the right to rent for a house let to the plaintiff for a year, submitted to arbitration in the tenant's presence; the court held the tenant was bound by the arbitrators' award without separate notice since he was privy to the submission.
notes: The underlying transaction is an ordinary year-long house letting, but the case turns entirely on arbitration and notice between two competing claimants to the rent, not on the character or regulation of lodging/boarding occupancy.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Trespass for unlawful entry into a dwelling house; the court held that while keeping an inn gives a general implied license to enter, the plaintiff's house was not shown to be an inn, so the defendant's uninvited entry and refusal to leave was a trespass.
notes: States the innkeeper implied-license-to-enter doctrine, but the house at issue was expressly found not to be an inn and no letting or boarding transaction is at issue; case is about trespass, not compensated occupancy or its regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Action for use and occupation of a lot and dwelling house after the original lease term expired; the court held that because the original rent was reserved on the bare lot only, a tenant holding over after the landlord acquired title to buildings erected during the term must pay the higher value of land and buildings, not the old ground rent.
notes: Use-and-occupation rent valuation dispute after lease expiration; ordinary landlord-tenant law, not lodging or boarding.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Assumpsit for rent of a house and lot where the tenant, after his lease expired, attorned to a mortgagee whose mortgage had been forfeited; the court held a tenant of a mortgagor may lawfully attorn to the mortgagee after forfeiture and set this up as a defense against the mortgagor's rent claim.
notes: Mortgagor/mortgagee attornment and rent-privity dispute over a leased house; no lodging or boarding issue.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Replevin over a cider mill and press built by a tenant from year to year on a farm; the court held such machinery remained the tenant's personal property, removable at the end of the tenancy.
notes: Fixtures dispute between farm landlord and tenant; unrelated to lodging or boarding.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Motion to set aside a partition report between tenants in common of a woollen factory; the court confirmed the commissioners' treatment of loose, unattached machinery as personal property rather than realty.
notes: Fixtures/partition dispute over factory machinery; unrelated to lodging or boarding.

court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
holding_summary: Procedural ruling holding that a landlord seeking ejectment for non-payment of rent on unoccupied demised premises, where the tenant cannot be served personally, must proceed under the statutory summary proceedings rather than by affixing a declaration on the premises.
notes: Purely procedural ejectment-service ruling; no lodging or boarding issue.

holding_summary: Replevin/avowry dispute over a landlord's right to distrain under a parol lease for years; the court held a void parol demise for a term of years enures as a tenancy from year to year, sufficient to support distress for rent.
notes: General landlord-tenant distress/parol-lease doctrine (facts not specified beyond a house and lot rented at $140/year); not specific to lodging or boarding.

holding_summary: Trover action addressing whether a landlord could distrain for rent absent an express clause of distress; the court held a landlord with a reversionary interest may distrain at common law under the tenure of free and common socage, without needing statutory authority.
notes: General property-law doctrine on rent service/charge/seek and fealty; not specific to lodging or boarding.

holding_summary: Action against a deputy sheriff for seizing horses that a neighbor had left with an innkeeper for feeding and keeping; the court held the innkeeper had no lien because the horse owner was never a 'guest,' and the innkeeper's extraordinary liability and lien attach only where the goods' owner is actually or constructively a guest.
notes: Extensively discusses innkeeper liability and 'guest' status doctrine, but the property at issue is horses boarded at a stable/inn (agistment), not human lodgers or the letting of rooms/dwellings for pay; not on-topic for the corpus's human-occupancy focus.
